claims.text: The initial material is a single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy.
A nanoscale oxide dispersion is to be introduced as a secondary phase.
The targeted oxide volume fraction is 5 vol%.
The targeted oxide particle size is 10 nm.
The alloy and oxide dispersion can be produced by powder metallurgy with mechanical alloying.
The oxide dispersion will pin magnetic domain walls.
The oxide dispersion will reduce magnetic domain size.
Pinning by the oxide particles reduces domain-wall mobility and raises the energy required for domain-wall motion.
Smaller magnetic domains require more energy to reverse their magnetization.
Adding the oxide dispersion will increase coercivity by at least 50% relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
The modified alloy will have a coercive field of at least 150 Oe.
The oxide dispersion will reduce saturation magnetization by no more than 10%.
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy has a coercive field of 100 Oe.
The baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi alloy has a saturation magnetization of 1.2 T.
An oxide content of 2–10 vol% is expected to provide pinning while avoiding excessive loss of saturation magnetization.
An oxide particle-size range of 5–20 nm is expected to optimize the balance between domain-wall pinning and saturation magnetization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis separately predicts both a coercivity increase of at least 50% and saturation magnetization within 10% of baseline, but the falsification rule requires both predictions to fail simultaneously. Thus failure of the primary coercivity prediction alone would not falsify the hypothesis under the stated rule.
